messages:
maya: Morning — dropping the perf dump from last night (kernel flip + burst load). p95 stayed ~120ms but p99 jumped to ~820ms when the request queue spiked. need opinions on target util and whether we should do soft admit or aggressive shedding.

sam: link?

maya: https://internal.redwood/runs/216789 — key bits below:
```
kernel_strategy: auto-flip
microbatch_size: 4
target_util: 0.78
avg_gpu_util: 81%
throughput: 18k tokens/s
p95: 118ms
p99: 820ms (tail events coinciding with kvmiss + kernel switch)
queue_depth at spike: ~72 requests
```

kai: so tail is correlated with kvmiss + kernel handoff. are we warming kvs before switching kernels?

maya: no, handoff happens on first request after flip. kvmiss penalty ~180ms, kernel init ~140ms, they compound in the tail.

jules: my gut — current target_util=0.78 is too close to saturation if rare kernel flips cost ~300ms. consider soft-admit to keep utilization ~0.62-0.68.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job created for shadow-admit-policy (id: canary-216789) — monitors p95/p99 and queue_len.

ankit: also watch short-session traffic: KV warmup dominates for <64-token requests. If we drop target_util too low we'll lose throughput; maybe do adaptive headroom: lower util when kvmiss_rate > X.

sam: agree with adaptive headroom. can we add a quick heuristic: if kvmiss_rate > 0.03 then target_util := max(0.62, target_util - 0.12)?

jules: and add a short-circuit: when kernel_flip_count in last 60s > 2 -> temporarily pin kernel to current variant for 30s to avoid repeated in-flight handoffs.

jen: propose experiment plan:
- shadow-admit for 48h (no user-visible rejects).
- metric guards: alarm if p99 > 420ms for >5m or queue_len > 64 for >3m.
- collect: p50/p95/p99, kvmiss_rate, kernel_flip_rate, avg_gpu_util, tail_event_count.
- safety rollback: auto-disable policy if any guard fires.

maya: can we also log per-request tags: "kvmiss", "kernel_flip", "prefetch_hit" so we can segment tail events?

ankit: yes, add those tags at admission time + kernel switch hook. will add counters.

sam: measurement dashboards: add a small perf panel: stacked timeline of p99, kvmiss_rate, kernel_flip_rate, and avg_gpu_util. annotate when canary toggles.

ops-bot: perf-pipeline: ingest started for canary-216789, retention 7d.

maya: action items:
- ankit: add per-request tags + adaptive headroom heuristic (kv-based).
- jules: implement kernel pin short-circuit.
- sam: dashboard + alert rules.
- jen: create canary run config (shadow admit + alarms).
- maya: run canary EOD and check morning.

jen: i can own the canary config, will push proto by 6pm.

maya: thanks — want to avoid full-on shedding unless we see sustained p99 regressions. aim for graceful soft-admit first. :thumbsup:

sam: one more ask — can we add a tiny fallback to a smaller quantized model for shed events instead of just dropping? trade quality for latency.

maya: noted. i'll add that to the experiment as an optional fallback.

kai: cool — sounds like a plan.

maya: closing loop: will post results + slices after 48h.
